title: Conditional — Regular Conjugation
description: Express hypothetical situations and polite requests using the conditional tense.

vocabulary.source: could you / you would be able to
she told me she would come

grammar.title: Conditional (Condicional Simple) — Regular Conjugation
grammar.content:
The conditional expresses what 'would' happen — it's used for polite requests, hypothetical situations, and reported speech. The conditional is remarkably easy: take the FULL infinitive as the stem and add these endings:

Conditional endings (add to the full infinitive):
- yo: -ía
- tú: -ías
- él/ella/usted: -ía
- nosotros: -íamos
- vosotros: -íais
- ellos/ellas/ustedes: -ían

Examples:
- hablar → hablaría, hablarías, hablaría, hablaríamos, hablaríais, hablarían
- comer → comería, comerías, comería, comeríamos, comeríais, comerían
- vivir → viviría, vivirías, viviría, viviríamos, viviríais, vivirían

Notice: the conditional endings (-ía, -ías, -ía...) are EXACTLY the same as the imperfect -ER/-IR endings. Context tells you which tense is being used.
examples: Me gustaría visitar México un día. (I would like to visit Mexico one day.)
¿Podrías ayudarme con esto? (Could you help me with this?)
Si tuviera dinero, compraría una casa. (If I had money, I would buy a house.)
Ella me dijo que vendría. (She told me she would come.)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian conditional also uses the particle 'aș/ai/ar/ăm/ăți/ar' + infinitive: 'aș vorbi' (I would speak). Spanish is structurally different — it fuses everything into one word. Both languages use the conditional for polite requests: 'Could you...?'.

grammar.title: Conditional — Irregular Stems (Same as Future)
grammar.content:
The conditional shares the same irregular stems as the future tense, but uses the conditional endings (-ía, -ías, etc.) instead. This means the stem changes are memorized once and applied to both tenses:

- tener → tendría (I would have)
- poner → pondría (I would put)
- salir → saldría (I would leave)
- poder → podría (I would be able to)
- querer → querría (I would want)
- decir → diría (I would say)
- hacer → haría (I would do/make)
- saber → sabría (I would know)
- venir → vendría (I would come)
- caber → cabría (I would fit)
examples: ¿Podría pedirle un favor? (Could I ask you a favor?)
Ella diría la verdad. (She would tell the truth.)
Si pudiera, viajaría a Japón. (If I could, I would travel to Japan.)
No sabría responder esa pregunta. (I wouldn't know how to answer that question.)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian conditional also uses the same irregular stem change: 'aș avea' (I would have) uses 'avea' as the stem. Spanish 'tendría' uses 'tendr-' as the stem. The Romanian 'aș' + infinitive is two words where Spanish uses one.

pronunciation.title: The Vowel Sound in Conditional -ía
pronunciation.content:
Conditional endings all carry the stress on the -í:

- yo: -ía (stress on the í: ha-blar-ÍA)
- tú: -ías (ha-blar-ÍAS)
- él/ella/usted: -ía (ha-blar-ÍA)
- nosotros: -íamos (ha-blar-Ía-MOS)
- vosotros: -íais (ha-blar-Ía-IS)
- ellos/ellas/ustedes: -ían (ha-blar-ÍAN)

The conditional endings are written with accents because they contain a stressed 'í'. This is the visual difference between the imperfect -ER/-IR and the conditional — both share the same sounds but the conditional always has the accent on the 'i'.

Critical: Spanish 'comería' is pronounced 'ko-me-RI-a' (four distinct syllables), NOT 'ko-MEER-yah' as English speakers might assume. The 'i' and 'a' in -ía are two separate syllables.
pronunciation.aid_note: Romanian vowel pronunciation is very similar to Spanish — pure vowels without diphthongs. The main challenge is the Spanish conditional -ía which has four syllables. Practice by stretching: 'ri-aaa' — two separate sounds.

exercises.question: What does the conditional express?
options: What would happen in hypothetical situations
exercises.explanation: The conditional expresses what 'would' happen — used for polite requests, hypothetical situations, and reported speech.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Me ____ (gustar) visitar Japón algún día.' (I would like to visit Japan one day.)
exercises.explanation: 'Gustaría' — conditional of gustar. Conditional of -AR verbs uses -ía endings.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Si tuviera dinero, yo ____ (comprar) una casa.' (If I had money, I would buy a house.)
exercises.explanation: 'Compraría' — conditional of comprar. Hypothetical 'si' clause: if I had... I would buy.

exercises.question: Complete: '¿____ (you) abrir la ventana?' (Could you open the window?)
exercises.explanation: 'Podrías' — conditional of poder for tú. This is a polite request.

exercises.question: Complete the conditional tense conjugation table for the regular verb ESTUDIAR:
exercises.explanation: Conditional tense adds endings directly to the full infinitive: estudiaría, estudiarías, estudiaría, estudiaríamos, estudiaríais, estudiarían.

exercises.question: What is the conditional of 'decir' for 'vosotros'?
exercises.explanation: 'Diríais' — decir uses the irregular stem dir- in the conditional: dir + íais = diríais.
